Seminar Title:

Vertex-minimal graphs and fixing sets for certain finite groups

Abstract: 

Every finite group can be represented as the automorphism group of some graph. So we have a question that,  given a finite group G, what is the smallest number of vertices of among all graphs with an automorphism group isomorphic to G? In this direction, we construct planar graphs whose automorphism group is isomorphic to an abelian group. Consequently, we obtain suitable upper bounds for vertex-minimal planar graphs with given abelian groups. Further, we classify all finite abelian groups for which these planar graphs are also vertex-minimal graphs.

	We consider a family of groups called modular p-groups. We compute the order of vertex-minimal graphs with an automorphism group isomorphic to a modular p-group. The fixing number of a graph is defined as the smallest number of vertices in that graph that, when fixed, makes the automorphism group trivial. For a finite group G, the fixing set is defined as the set of all fixing numbers of graphs having automorphism groups isomorphic to G. We show that fixing set of a modular p-group is {1}. A finite non-abelian group H is hamiltonian if all of its subgroups are normal. We compute the minimal orders of graphs having a hamiltonian group as their automorphism group. Further, we obtain the fixing sets corresponding to finite hamiltonian groups.

	Let G be a permutation group acting on a finite set S. The base of permutation representation in G is a subset B of S such that the stab(B) is trivial. The base size of that permutation is defined as the cardinality of the smallest base. The base size set is defined as the set of all base sizes of all faithful representations of G on finite sets. We conduct a comparative study between the fixing sets and the base size sets of different classes of finite groups. We prove that for the dihedral group, the base size set and the fixing set are not equal. In contrast, for several other groups, the base size set coincides with the fixing set.
